implemented.elk: web/vite.config.ts aliases ^elkjs(/.*)?$ to web/src/lib/elkDisabled.ts (throws on construction); forbidElkjs Rollup plugin (web/scripts/forbid-elkjs.mjs) fails the build if any module id lies under node_modules/elkjs/ (verified: the build fails with the alias removed); web/scripts/check-no-elk.mjs scans the output for org.eclipse.elk.alg. and org.eclipse.elk.core. as a second layer (the generic wrapper names were dropped: they can appear in unrelated code, and forbidElkjs covers the wrappers by module id); dagre is requested through layoutForDiagram for flowchart, state, class, ER and requirement diagrams and left unset for mind maps (Mermaid 12.1 would otherwise default them to ELK)
implemented.ci: Portal .github/workflows/licence.yml (dedicated workflow; push to main and integration/app-platform, pull requests, dispatch; Go SBOM for all six release platforms; npm production SBOM; ELK build test; scan); Apps .github/workflows/check.yml job licence (Go SBOM for the six status release targets; npm production SBOM; check_licence_copy.py; scan with --workspace-root)
implemented.apps_declarations: root, @portal-app/sdk, portal-status-ui, portal-symbols-demo and the status acceptance harness package.json declare AGPL-3.0-only; scripts/tests/test_licence_scan.py fails if one stops
implemented.reviewed_as: Per-component reviewed-as records pinned to the SHA-256 of the licence file read from the Go module cache or node_modules in CI, and to the exact declared expression; a changed hash, changed declaration, missing file or version mismatch makes the record stale and the gate fails again; a record cannot override a denied licence
implemented.nested_components: Components are walked recursively; one component is judged once only when bom-ref, version and declared licences are identical, conflicting copies are each judged
implemented.own_workspace: An own component needs a purl; Go a pkg:golang purl; npm an install path of exactly node_modules/<name>, no registry distribution and membership of the repository's npm workspaces (--workspace-root)
implemented.elections: Elections are evidence: declaration pinned exactly and by kind; offered expression a pure top-level OR with the elected licence an operand and allowed (allow list or election_only); no denied or unallowed extra operand; pinned to the SHA-256 of the licence files that ship (dompurify LICENSE and LICENSE-MPL, golang/freetype LICENSE); a changed or missing file makes the election stale
implemented.licence_files: npm licence file read from the SBOM's install path (cdx:npm:package:path); installed package.json version must equal the component version; roots escaping node_modules or the module cache are refused; licence entries with only a url or text fail as unknown
implemented.copy_check: Apps scripts/check_licence_copy.py (public repositories, anonymous or with the workflow's read-only GITHUB_TOKEN sent only to api.github.com): the copy equals the Portal commit in scripts/licence-scan.pin; the pin is reachable from a live Portal branch (integration/app-platform or main, live = carries the file); the pinned files equal at least one live branch; a branch that contains the pin but lost the file fails; before any branch has the file only the pin is compared. The pin is 9fac73ef7b8c4f614b3595595b92f71936a5afd1, a feature-branch commit, to be moved to the merge commit after the Portal PR merges
implemented.mermaid_turn: Each diagram's mermaid.initialize, parse and render run as one turn on a module-level promise chain (web/src/lib/mermaidTurn.ts), so its layout and theme are in force for its own render; tests render a flowchart and a mind map concurrently in both orders; a turn is rejected after 15 seconds so a render that never settles cannot stall later diagrams (its block keeps the source as a code block)
implemented.lock_cross_check: With --node-modules, every installed npm component's declaration must equal its installed package.json (license string or object, legacy licenses list, several as a set), read from the SBOM's install path with the version checked; mismatch fails as lock-mismatch and no record covers it; untrustworthy installs fail as lock-unverifiable; own and Go components are skipped; components not installed (optional packages of other platforms) are judged on the lock and counted in a warning. An installed-tree SBOM (no --package-lock-only) was tried and gives a different component set (328 against 347), so the SBOM stays lock-based

limits: Source and lock inputs only: no released binary or OCI digest has been scanned; the release-key and environment approval remain open.

The licence detector assigns BSD-Source-Code to the Go BSD 3-clause text; the reviewed-as record, pinned to the file hash, covers the seven Portal modules and two in Apps. A new golang.org/x module is not covered until the owner adds it.
apps/status/tests (not shipped) and templates/react-app (no lockfile) are not scanned.
golang/freetype's dual licence is evidenced by the LICENSE in the module cache at the pinned hash; a new freetype version with a different LICENSE needs the election re-pinned by the owner.

The Apps copy check compares with a Portal commit and the live Portal branches; until the Portal PR merges the pin is a feature-branch commit, and after a squash merge it must be moved to the merge commit or the check fails (intended).

The lock cross-check covers installed packages only; the optional packages of other platforms are judged on the lock's declaration (19 in the Portal SBOM on a macOS machine) and are not part of what ships.
